review: הַלְלוּיָהּ opens every stanza, as هَلِّلُويَا does in the Arabic; it is left untranslated, as in the Psalter and in hymn 74.

1:3–1:4 כָּלָה זִקַּתְנוּ / לֶעָפָר וְלַבָּשָׂר — 'our kinship with dust and flesh has ended'; the Arabic نِسْبَتُنَا لِلتُّرَابِ وَالْجَسَد is a single construct, and זִקָּה is the post-biblical noun for a legal bond, chosen because the clause needs a subject.
2:2 נִצְדַּקְנוּ בוֹ — Romans 5:1 (נִצְדַּקְנוּ מִן־הָאֱמוּנָה); the Arabic فَتَبَرَّرْنَا بِهِ is 'we were justified', and the niphal of צדק is the fixed term.

3:2 קַמְנוּ אִתּוֹ בְּיֶדַע — 'we rose with Him in certainty', for قُمْنَا مَعَهُ بِالْيَقِين; בְּיֶדַע ('with knowledge') is used for the Arabic's بِالْيَقِين because יֶדַע also carries 'certain knowledge' in liturgical usage.
3:3 כָּלָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט — 'judgment has ended'; the Arabic دَيْنُونَةٌ is the condemnation of Rom 8:1, and מִשְׁפָּט is the biblical noun for it.
